questions.prompt: A friend asks you an obscure question about Islam that you genuinely don't know. Which response best matches Islamic intellectual ethics?
options: Offer your best guess so you do not look uninformed
Say "I do not know" honestly instead of guessing
Change the subject and hope they forget
questions.explanation: Saying "I do not know" honestly is the habit taught in Nahj al-Balagha Saying 82.

questions.prompt: Which statement about God appears in Surah al-Ikhlas (112)?
options: He has a partner who shares His rule
He neither begat, nor was begotten, nor has He any equal
He is one power among many
questions.explanation: Surah al-Ikhlas ends: He neither begat, nor was begotten, nor has He any equal.

questions.prompt: Someone argues that God must live in a specific physical place in the sky to be "near" to humans. How does Imam Ali describe this in Sermon 1?
options: God is near only to people who travel to certain places
God is far from creation in every sense
God is near to creation without physical contact and distinct without physical distance
questions.explanation: Sermon 1 says He is with everything but not in physical nearness, and different from everything but not in physical separation.

questions.prompt: In a diverse society, what bond does Nahj al-Balagha Letter 53 say you share with someone who does not follow your religion?
options: No bond at all
Equal dignity as a fellow human being in creation
A bond of rivalry
questions.explanation: Letter 53 says people are either your brother in religion or one like you in creation.

questions.prompt: You read a single Qur'an verse that seems puzzling on its own. What is the first method Al-Mizan uses to understand it?
options: Choose the reading that sounds best to you
Read it alongside related verses across the Qur'an and within its chapter's unified theme
Rely on one popular opinion
questions.explanation: Al-Mizan explains the Qur'an with the help of the Qur'an itself.

questions.prompt: According to Surah al-'Alaq 96:6-7, what can happen when a person considers himself without need?
options: He becomes more careful
He becomes rebellious
He becomes more generous
questions.explanation: The verse says man becomes rebellious when he considers himself without need.

questions.prompt: When early Muslims were persecuted in Makkah, why did Prophet Muhammad send a group to a Christian kingdom in Ethiopia?
options: Because it was the nearest country to Makkah
Because its people already followed the Prophet
Because its ruler was known for justice and protecting people from oppression
questions.explanation: The Message, Chapter 17: a mighty and just ruler, under whom nobody is oppressed.

questions.prompt: A solar eclipse occurred the day the Prophet's infant son Ibrahim died, and people assumed the sky was mourning him. How did the Prophet respond?
options: He accepted it as a sign of his greatness
He corrected them publicly, explaining that eclipses follow natural laws and do not occur for anyone's birth or death
He asked people not to speak about it
questions.explanation: The Message, Chapter 55: the sun and moon are not eclipsed on account of anyone's death or birth.

questions.prompt: According to Surah ar-Ra'd 13:28, where do hearts find rest?
options: In remembrance of Allah
In wealth and rank
In constant distraction
questions.explanation: The verse says the hearts find rest in Allah's remembrance.

questions.prompt: Surah Al 'Imran 3:134 describes the virtuous as those who do what with their anger?
options: Let it grow
Pass it on to others
Suppress it
questions.explanation: The verse describes those who suppress their anger and excuse the faults of the people.

questions.prompt: Surah al-Baqarah 2:156 gives the words the patient say when an affliction visits them. Which are they?
options: Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him do we indeed return
Why has this happened to me?
Nothing can be done now
questions.explanation: The verse gives: Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him do we indeed return.

questions.prompt: What does the first clause of Surah al-Baqarah 2:256 say about religion?
options: Religion may be enforced
There is no compulsion in religion
Religion is a private matter for scholars
questions.explanation: The verse opens: There is no compulsion in religion.

questions.prompt: Surah Al 'Imran 3:7 calls the definitive verses "the mother of the Book". What is a careful way to read one unclear line?
options: Build a rule from it at once
Look at the clearer verses and its surrounding passage first
Share it before checking anything
questions.explanation: The clause points to the definitive verses as the core of the Book, so context comes first.

questions.prompt: According to Surah al-Hujurat 49:6, what should you do with news brought by a vicious character?
options: Verify it
Pass it on quickly
Believe it if it is exciting
questions.explanation: The verse says: verify it, lest you visit harm on some people out of ignorance.
